verdict.tagline: Familiar survival mechanics clash with sparse maps and abandoned updates.
for_you_if: you want portable sessions on deck hardware
you like hunting for broken synergies
not_for_you_if: you dislike heavy reliance on luck

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players appreciate smooth performance while noting early signs of repetition and heavy luck dependence.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs well on the Steam deck.

citations.review_text: This is addictive. Very much like risk of rain 2. I think risk of rain 2 is more skill oriented, but this still takes skill. It is also like vampire survivor but takes more skill. its an interesting mix and something that lives perfectly on steam deck. i really enjoyed this, once i beat the tier 3 boss once i kinda lost interest which is ok, was a fun little game for 7$.

The game is fun on my steam deck when I’m travelling. Only big thing to consider before buying is that 70% of the unlockable items are inherently bad and once they are added to the loot pool the game becomes increasingly difficult and I liked that but most people won’t. Progression makes the game harder. I definitely got my monies worth with time played but I only played it while traveling. I wouldn’t play this on my PC with everything else that’s available.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks content or variety after extended play.

citations.review_text:
Having played every survivors game out there, I'm afraid to say that this one might be the best. I keep coming back to it, my kids love watching it, chasing all the unlocks is challenging, the stages are challenging. Graveyard's level designs was a nice change of pace, and the final boss fight was great. Like all survivors games, it's extremely thin on content - I would love for there to be many more levels, enemy types, and bosses. There's already a good amount of weapons and playable characters. 

This is like Risk of Rain but without the "FPS"/precision gameplay. Much more chill and fun for me. Highly recommend

At $10 Megabonk is a fine purchase. It's not a great game. But it's a decent $10 game, which is the only reason I'm recommending it. I burned out on this at around 18 hours of play. There's just not enough variety to keep me hooked past that. It's fun for a few memes, though.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking in plot or story.

citations.review_text: No plot, no deep thinking, zero brain cells required. You start off totally panicking, and 10 minutes later you’re an absolute god vaporizing everything on the map. It’s just pure, stupid fun.

Easy-to-pickup twin sticker shooter that you can spend hours playing! Its low poly PS1/N64 graphics are charming, the character designs and items descriptions are funny/quirky, and there's a lot of depth/replay ability to the combat with each character having different abilities + weapon variety per run. Best part is that this game is only $10 (with no discount) and can run on potato PCs. Megabonk is a reminder that games don't need to have the most high-end cream of the crop graphics to be fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game feels repetitive over time.

citations.review_text:
Mega Bonk is a fun and chaotic game that takes a simple idea and makes it surprisingly addictive. The goal is easy: smash enemies, collect upgrades, and become the ultimate bonking machine. The fast gameplay, goofy animations, and satisfying hits make every fight entertaining.

The game’s colorful visuals and ridiculous power-ups give it a lot of personality. Unlocking new abilities keeps things interesting, and the constant action makes it easy to jump in for a quick session.

While the gameplay can get repetitive after a while, Mega Bonk is still a great choice if you want a silly, relaxing game where you can just have fun and cause chaos. It may not be the most complex game out there, but its charm and humor make it worth playing.

Let me know if you want me to change the tone, make it more serious, more funny, or adjust the length. I can also rewrite it to sound more like a professional game critic or a casual player review.
great game. only problem i'd say is that it's a bit repetitive, but that's hard to fix.
The numbers go up, sure, but the gameplay stays quite repetitive.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay loop and runs as heavily dependent on luck and RNG.

citations.review_text: This game's sense of humor is genuinely cringe-inducing, and actively ruins any semblance of tone it otherwise had. It's the first thing I brought up because it's unfortunately the most memorable thing about this game. There's honestly not much else to talk about anyway; it's boring and sometimes frustrating not being able to control where I'm shooting, the gameplay loop is generally unsubstantial and luck-dependent, and I can already tell the overall content is sorely lacking. I can't deny it's pretty reliable at delivering that low-maintenance dopamine, but let's be so real... there's nothing else it really has to offer.
It's good, but it's genuinely worse Vampire Surviors. The RNG is horrendous. Once you start unlocking items, you realise exactly how RNG-dependent a run is, which is mildly infuriating.
too much Rng and luck based makes it to where its just a restart simulator till you get a certain drop

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-journey players encounter sparse map selections, vertical enemy stacking, and strict RNG demands.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game currently features a very small selection of maps and lacks updates or new content.

citations.review_text:
I legitimately had a great time playing this game. It's essentially a 3D platformer version of Vampire Survivors; a game I also thoroughly enjoyed for many hours. I was really excited to have been here when it was new and full of promise...

.........but now, it just sits there. The most "recent" content for the game is just hats, it still hasn't been patched/fixed from it's current janky state from the last REAL content release which forces you to play said level only one way (and therefore completely upends the whole creative freedom thing it HAD going until that point), and we've heard nothing of any future plans regarding it in over half a year. 

This is a game full of potential, but it appears to have been abandoned shortly after release. You'll get some good fun out of it for a time, but if you're looking for something with extended replayability I'd suggest looking elsewhere, like Vampire Survivors or something similar.
Dead game :( the dev dropped off the face of the earth and now there's no updates :*(
unfinished game, it's a scam atm, only 2 worlds with 3 stages + 1 world and some challenges. (most of them repeat themselves), some items are useless, some are broken.
Was once a great game. Its now abandoned. Developer made gang cash off memes, took our money and just left the project.
Fun game but unfortunately its abandoned so, its up to you if you want to spend a dime on it

Really really fun and addicting, you can easily loose a few hours without noticing. It's very similar to vampire survivors, so if you like that you'll also like this.
It's easy to get into while still being mechanically complex (requiring a good knowledge of how the game works to master it). There's a good variety of weapons, tomes, items and, consequently, builds that make it interesting and engaging to play, but it's a bit lacking in maps (only 3 at the moment of writing).
One of the best of its genre.

Was okay while it lasted. There has been no new update since January, it feels like the dev already gave up on this game. Will change my review if they ever release something new, but for now, my hopes for this game's future are pretty low. Playing the same two maps with the same perks and the same characters over and over again gets old pretty fast.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe issues with enemies stacking vertically or spawning directly underneath the player, leading to unavoidable damage and unfair deaths.

citations.review_text:
I dont understad the lobe for this one. After a little while I simply felt like i was playing an unfinished and broken game. 

Physics are garbage, enemies constantly walk through walls out of your attack range. I-frames do not exist and enemies are overpowered from the start so you can be killed in 10 seconds simoly because the game spawned somewhere you cant even see above your head in the first ten seconds of gameplay and fell down on you and touched you 3 times.

The broken mechanics everywhere in this game made me not even want to continue.

At some point, the enemies in this game began to default to stacking vertically.  Not only do enemies jump to stack, some enemies have higher jumps such that the highest stack I have seen was eight enemies tall.  These stacks are extremely difficult to fight because the enemies above can drop on drop on the player character to deal constant, high damage.  This was bad enough before enemies began to jump on the player character directly such that a newly-spawned enemy could end a run at pretty much any time.  Weapons do not attack vertically, and the ones which have some vertical aspect to their hitboxes are insufficient to deal with this problem.

I almost forgot to mention that the Anubis boss's hitbox is so much larger than its model that to use AOE weapons is to invite death.

There are some cool highlights when everything just clicks and works together. But holy moly is that rare and most games you are scrounging for a shred of luck going your way. I really tried to give this a chance but im about to pull my hair with this RNG. Enemies snipe you even though i am zooming across the map, you get some cool items and it seems to go your way but you never quite get the ones you need to pop-off. 

Early game is the worst cause youre spending so much time trying to get the build pieces and when it comes its usually too late and the enemy just overpowers you. Enemies often spawn directly under you if you are flying around and when a few surround you, it doesnt matter cause the hits slow you and you cant escape. 

It feels very little skill or input is involved and its just sheer, luck and hopefully you dont land on a spawned enemy. bosses often have attacks that cant be avoided

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that power-ups and items lack detailed explanations of what they actually do.

citations.review_text: Great game, just wish the power-ups would give you a little more detail in what they do

The opening hours were great. Characters seemed unique, movement was fun to perform and a good run really made you feel strong. I still feel like each characters level-up bonuses provide a strong baseline to experiment. I don't mind the humour. It's not too distracting. You might lose a little of its charm if you don't mess with it, but it doesn't make or break the game.

However, when you get into optimising builds, you then realise there's practical limits on how creative you can be. Certain items, tomes and weapons were always the 'correct' choice and others were always 'wrong'. Unlocking items felt quite grindy, making every run feel like a trudge to get them. Plus, the system which removes items from the pool is limited only to items you unlock, meaning the items you want are still diluted by everything else.

It's unfair to compare different games, but having played Risk of Rain 2 and Vampire Survivors, I really expected to enjoy this game more than I did. This is all subject to change when a new update is out, but for now, I can't see myself returning to this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the final boss as exceptionally annoying to fight on several heroes.

citations.review_text:
In general there's a good game underneath some questionable design choices. The rng is very heavy in this one and stacked against you. Having beat it the last boss is exceptionally annoying an boring to fight on several heroes. Especially if you boosted your movement speed.

On the topic of movement speed, most heroes move slow as hell as if stuck in molasses and need heavy investment in movement speed pickups to feel even half decent to play, very frustrating.

Sometimes the end portal simply dosen't spawn, killing your run unjustly.

In this genre i'd suggest getting risk of rain 2 instead. WHile that one also has some bugs it dosen't feel as sluggish as this one.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight minimal biomes, halted developer support, and rigid meta dependencies.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features only three maps or biomes.

citations.review_text:
This game is crazy stuff!

Is almost like a meme game with a goofy vibe and being as cheap as it is, I didn't expect at all for it to be so much fun!

On paper it may seem limited with only 3 types of maps/biomes but that's irrelevant. There are lots of characters and weapons available, allowing you to try lots of viable builds. 

This is the book example of a "one more run" type of game that somehow will keep you hooked for more than 100 hours easily (I know it did with me, I "just" wanted to unlock everything)

The music is also very good. Usually I mute the music on most games and put on other music or podcast, but with this game is worth leaving the music on, you'll vibe with it!

Some bad things you must take in mind:
- Sometimes may be very hard (oh wait, that's a good thing)

Jokes asides, the real bad thing about this game is that development seems to be finished and the game still had so much potential to go! The could have added more maps, more game modes (like the 3rd map that plays different than the first and second), more characters and more weapons. Is a shame but at least you can't complain how much hours of fun you're getting for such a cheap price

I really want to love this game, but it's heavily carried by just giving dopamine. If you don't get your exact weapons and tomes right away then it's really frustrating. Rerolling level upgrades costs gold for whatever reason. You get all of these tomes and weapons you don't want right away so you have to either waste rerolls if you can or just die since doing good damage is impossible when you don't have your 4 weapons. It really should just be pick the weapons and tomes right away so you don't waste levels on things you're never going to use. As many have mentioned in reviews the characters, weapons, and tomes are very unbalanced. When I'm playing a videogame I'm looking for strategy and not how lucky I can get, since I haven't even mentioned items, the 3 maps, and the huge ramp in difficulty scaling.  Having 10 keys which give 10% each shouldn't have me feeling like I have only have 5. There is definitely a cap for keys, but the game doesn't communicate caps most of the time. I hope this game gets updated and fixed, but it's been half a year since the last update from when I'm writing this, and no clear plans from the dev for the future. If Vedinad is who people are saying he is, ghosting fans of his creations is usual. I wouldn't give my hopes up that this game or any future game from Vedinad will be updated if it's incomplete

Is it repetitive? Yes. Is it fun? Also yes.

Megabonk is one of the few games I keep coming back to because, even though it isn’t super difficult or packed with a ton of different mechanics, it’s still fun trying to beat your previous run. That’s especially true when you’re using a character you already know well, or even one that doesn’t have the best attack style or movement. There’s something satisfying about seeing how much better you can do each time.

Plus, there are a ton of achievements to unlock, and that’s always a big plus for me personally.

My only real hope is that they add more maps. It’s been a while since the game has had any major updates, and at the time of this review, there are still only three total maps. The game could definitely use more biomes, new modes, or something fresh to give Megabonk another spark of life.

Very good roguelike, and a banger when it was released, but the time its killing this game.
The lack of support for Non-Meta build and more content generate that less people its playing this game or leaving it before completing the "end-game experience".
Also the dev ghosted so don't expected more content, now he is rich with a budget game.

Update: This game is bad. It is so damn frustrating with the amount of bs you have to put up with. So many good runs that are ruined due to rng, difficulty spikes, etc. Runs that would have likely been your high score/leaderboard worthy gone.

So many garbage/bad items/tomes/weapons that you will banish/skip/reroll, but don't use those options up cause there are moai and shady traders that you want to skip/reroll too. At most you have 7 max for each for the ENTIRE RUN. Yeah if rng sucks you will run out of those extremely fast.

Damage enemies deal is stupid. Even with a small amount of difficulty % they will take most of your hp. Like 30% diff elites will deal 55ish damage. On a squishy character that's almost 1/2 of your hp.

Original review:
It's very middle of the road for me. There are good/fun aspects, and bad/frustrating parts that make me hesitant to recommend (unless it's on sale then it's good). The game seems to be abandoned now and is just left in it's current state. The current bad points are:

- Kinda boring? It's mainly to due luck/rng. There are some really fun/good runs you will have, but also a lot of mediocre/bad ones. So much of it is rng based and while there are ways to slim the rng aspects, it's not enough. Also there are meta builds that are obviously the way to play if you want to get high scores. Too bad it's so restrictive.

- Enemies and bosses are pretty lame. All of them walk toward you with only a few normal enemies doing something "unique" like shooting a projectile or poisoning you. Bosses are better but still pretty lackluster.

- Bosses are bs. Bark Vader/Anubis is dumb since those 2 essentially give most builds the middle finger. An otherwise broken/op build is rendered useless cause the final boss is there, in your way. They take your other weapons until you beat the obelisk pha…

♥♥♥♥ game with mechanics.

pros
You can kill time with it if you are into rouguelike games and understand the basic concept of A roguelike. 
Cons 
* This game heavily and I mean heavily depends on only meta builds which varies from update to update. There's no experimenting with builds. 

P.s: 90% of Community members also get violently butthurt if you constructively criticize the game (maybe skill issue ?) which really contradicts the "Very Positive" state of the game. If I was making ♥♥♥♥ games regularly and I needed a cash, I would make cash grab slop like this and make a ruse about it. 

Worth it? 
Only buy it if you get it free on EPIC Games
